content: I feel anxious about whether I can pass my exams.

Academic pressure can feel relentless, especially when deadlines pile up all at once. Remember that your capacity on any given day doesn't define your intelligence or your future.

Try breaking down what's ahead into just the next 20 minutes. What is one small, manageable step you could take right now — or would taking a 10-minute breath first serve you better?
I feel hopeless and want to end my life.

I'm hearing how much pain and weight you're carrying right now, and I want you to know that you don't have to navigate this alone.

Because your safety and life matter deeply, please connect directly with people who are trained to support you through this exact moment. These free, confidential resources are available right now:

• **Tele-MANAS (Govt. of India)**: Dial `14416` or `1800-891-4416` (24x7, Toll-Free, Multiple Languages)
• **KIRAN Mental Health Helpline**: Dial `1800-599-0019` (24x7, Toll-Free)
• **iCall Psychosocial Helpline**: Call `9152987821` (Mon–Sat, 10 AM – 8 PM)
• **Vandrevala Foundation**: Call `9999 666 555` or WhatsApp available (24x7)
• **Emergency Services**: Dial `112` or visit your campus health clinic immediately.

Please consider reaching out to a friend, family member, or university counsellor today. You deserve care, understanding, and support.

I feel anxious about whether I can pass my exams.

Academic deadlines have a way of feeling like an avalanche where everything demands your focus at the exact same time. First, take a gentle breath: **Your worth as a human being is not measured by your grades or your daily productivity.**

When everything feels urgent, our brain freezes. Let's do a micro-triage: What is the single smallest assignment or slide deck you could look at for just **15 minutes** today? You don't have to finish it—just take that first step.

I'm having a hard time unwinding before sleep.

Sleep difficulties and university stress are deeply intertwined. When your mind has been running at high alert all day, it doesn't know how to simply 'switch off' when your head hits the pillow.

A gentle practice: If you've been tossing and turning for more than 20 minutes, don't force it. Sit in dim light, read something non-stimulating or listen to soft ambient sounds until drowsiness naturally visits.

Have late-night screens or caffeine been part of your evening routine lately?
